characters.continuity: Final Fantasy VII (1997 original) storyline; Final Fantasy VII Remake (2020) combat kit noted separately where stated
characters.summary: Magic-focused support caster. In the original game she wields staves that boost Magic, has high Magic and low physical stats, and her Limit Breaks are entirely defensive (healing and buffs). In Remake she is a ranged spellcaster who fires homing magical projectiles instead of striking with her staff.

techniques: Materia spellcasting; staves with many Materia slots boost her Magic (original)
Tempest: chargeable ranged magical attack (Remake)
Homing magical projectiles as her basic attack (Remake)
Arcane Ward: spells cast inside it are cast twice (Remake)

mechanisms: Defensive Limit Breaks: healing abilities and buffs (original)

weaknesses: Very low durability: lowest HP and Vitality in the Remake party
Was killed by a surprise attack while praying, when Sephiroth dropped from above and impaled her with the Masamune
limitations: Low physical stats; her strength is magic (original)

sources.supports: Original and Remake combat role, staves, Tempest, Arcane Ward, defensive Limits, low durability, death in the Forgotten City, and her role in Holy and the Lifestream stopping Meteor

feats.claim: Prayed at the Forgotten City altar to summon Holy with the White Materia; after her death her spirit commanded the Lifestream to push Meteor back so Holy could focus, and Holy and the Lifestream destroyed Meteor

notableResults.note: Not a fight: she was impaled with the Masamune while praying

campaignTags.claim: Magic-focused fighter who casts through Materia (original) and fights as a ranged spellcaster (Remake)
Her Limit Breaks are healing abilities and buffs for the party (original)

unknowns: Exact limits of her Ancient powers
The cited page does not describe individual Limits (Healing Wind, Great Gospel, Planet Protection) or Soul Drain; not claimed

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced Gemini's unsupported techniques (Soul Drain, Planet Protection), evasion, MP limitation and dodge-roll mobility with what the cited page states. Remake and Rebirth story divergence not covered.

characters.continuity: Hitman game series, single timeline (Codename 47 through Hitman 3 / World of Assassination); feats as summarized on the Hitman Wiki
characters.summary: Genetically enhanced clone assassin: master marksman, martial artist and knife thrower who infiltrates through disguise and blending into crowds, and uses Instinct to sense people through walls.

techniques: Fiber wire strangulation
Firearms marksmanship with pistols, shotguns, SMGs and rifles; one-handed pistol use and headshots at range
Knife throwing
Hand-to-hand: kickboxing, Panantukan, Krav Maga, Eskrima, Jiu-Jitsu; disarms armed soldiers
Poisons

mechanisms: Genetically enhanced strength, durability, speed and metabolism
Instinct: visualizes targets and guards through walls and floors

weaknesses: Susceptible to drugs and poisons: stabbed with a poisoned syringe (Blood Money), dosed by Diana's serum, and incapacitated by a remotely activated sedative (Hitman 3)
Serious wounds still need medical care (a bullet had to be removed)
limitations: Healing is described as limited, though sufficient
Enhancements are to peak physical condition

sources.supports: Skills and abilities, Instinct, vulnerabilities to serums and poison, and named targets and fights across the series

feats.claim: Was thrown through a wooden door by the superhumanly strong Sanchez and was knocked out for only a few minutes
Improvised a fiber wire from a windowsill and broom parts during an escape
Fought off the effects of Edwards's advanced memory-erasing serum
Infiltrated an ICA squadron disguised as an ICA trooper

notableResults.note: Killed with his bare hands despite Sanchez's superhuman strength

notableResults.citation: Hitman series (Hitman Wiki account), St. Petersburg
notableResults.note: Sent by Zavorotko to kill 47
Neck snapped in his office
Killed after 47 infiltrated his Chicago penthouse
Killed in Cornwall with his assistant Jade Nguyen
Killed or injected with the serum and stranded, by player choice
Assassinations, not open fights

campaignTags.claim: Infiltrated an ICA squadron disguised as an ICA trooper (Hitman 3); expert at disguise and blending into crowds

unknowns: Full extent of his genetic enhancements

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): Gemini's techniques, defenses and Instinct were restored where the Hitman Wiki supports them. Body armor, parkour, climbing and the generic 'ICA targets' result were dropped as unsupported. The page does not mention Silverballers. Some per-game citations follow the page's own section headings.

characters.continuity: Resident Evil main game series (Capcom), Code: Veronica (2000) through Resident Evil 5 (2009)
characters.summary: Virus-enhanced mastermind with superhuman strength, speed and agility since Code: Veronica. In Resident Evil 5 he effortlessly dodges and parries most attacks, and infects himself with Uroboros for his final form.

techniques: Superhuman strength, speed and agility in close combat
Uroboros tentacle arms that absorb and wield metallic objects as weapons (RE5 final form)

mechanisms: Effortlessly dodges and parries most attacks (RE5)

weaknesses: Injecting Serum PG67A/W into him after he is worn down is a required step in the RE5 tanker battle (Chapter 6-3)
Defeated by Chris Redfield in Code: Veronica and killed by Chris and Sheva in an active volcano in RE5
limitations: Uroboros is described as a volatile and mutagenic viral agent

sources.supports: Virus-enhanced strength, speed and agility, Uroboros, nigh-invincible dodging and parrying in RE5, defeat by Chris in Code: Veronica and death in RE5
Serum PG67A/W is used on Wesker once he keels over in the Chapter 6-3 tanker battle

feats.claim: Returned from his apparent death in the original Resident Evil with virus-enhanced strength, speed and agility

notableResults.note: Chris defeats him at the Antarctic facility
Killed in an active volcano after the serum step on the tanker

unknowns: Upper limit of his lifting strength
Regeneration and his need for regular serum injections are not stated by the opened sources; not claimed

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): the cited residentevil.fandom.com/wiki/Albert_Wesker page never came up in search and was not opened. It is replaced by Wikipedia and Evil Resource, both opened. The 'teleport-like' movement is reworded to superhuman speed.

techniques: Fire Breath
Frost Breath (used to drain melee fighters' stamina)
Roar that summons a meteor storm
Shout that resurrects dead dragons from burial mounds
Devours the souls of the dead to grow stronger

mechanisms: Cannot be damaged until Dragonrend grounds him (Skyrim)
Repeatedly restores the Sovngarde mist after it is cleared

weaknesses: Dragonrend: forces him to land and stay grounded, and is the only way to damage him
Elder Scroll banishment: Felldir read one to send him forward in time

Resurrected the dragon Sahloknir at Kynesgrove

Devoured souls in Sovngarde to strengthen himself

notableResults.note: Defeated and fled to Sovngarde

notableResults.opponent: Last Dragonborn with the three ancient heroes

Longsword and short blade
Throwing knives
Hand-to-hand combat
